provided in the constructor of the `FSM` actor (as opposed to attributes
of the data class).

In this commit, we separate the channel state from the context in which
the channel operates (which we could also call the Machine of the FSM).
For clarity, below is the gist of the change. The `State`/`Command`/
`Action` triplet remains the same, but we have a new `Context`, which
carries external context (node params, current block count, etc.).
Because `process` is now an _extension_ function of `Context`, it has
access to both the context and state data from its body. This is what
makes the change almost a drop-in replacement. Running a command on a
state is now slightly more complex, but it is also closer to the eclair
codebase.

```kotlin
sealed class Command {
    object Command1 : Command()
}

sealed class Action {
    object Action1 : Action()
}

sealed class State {

    abstract fun Context.process(cmd: Command): Pair<State, List<Action>>

    data class State1(val a: String) : State() {
        override fun Context.process(cmd: Command): Pair<State, List<Action>> {
            // we have access to both the context and the state
            val params = this.params
            val state = this@State1
            return State2(10) to listOf<Action.Action1>()
        }
    }

    data class State2(val b: Int) : State() {
        override fun Context.process(cmd: Command): Pair<State, List<Action>> {
            TODO("Not yet implemented")
        }
    }
}

data class Params(val alias: String)

data class Context(val params: Params)

fun test() {
    val context = Context(Params(alias = "my node"))
    val state = State.State1("foobar")

    val (state1, actions) = state.run { context.process(Command.Command1) }
}
```

Notes:
- overall there is less code than before because we remove unnecessary
data that we were carrying around for no reason
- end states like `Aborted` are now `object`s
- the channel state containing `currentTip` was misleading, because it
was not consistent with pending htlcs

* update tests

NB:
- got rid of `CurrentBlockCount` command entirely, it's not needed
  anymore since the block count is part of the context now
- a few tests have been ignored, it's easier to continue the rework of
serialization before fixing them

* factor and decouple serialization/encryption

It makes sense because:
- in the context of local persistence we use only serialization
- in the context of restore we use serialization + encryption

* add a new v4 serialization [no ci]

It uses a custom serialization, contrary to v2 and v3 which use
`kotlinx-serialization`.

The tradeoff for initially going with `kotlinx-serialization` was to
accept using a serialization mechanism that we don't fully control, in
exchange for more automation and less code. On top of that, we get json
serialization for free.

However, because channel data is so sensitive, we are not fully
confident in the serialization system (particularly w.r.t data model
migrations). In an attempt to reduce the risk of not being able to read
older data in the future, we have mirrored most of channel classes in
the `vX` packages, and we serialize those mirror classes, instead of the
actual ones.

We end up with well over a thousand lines of code for each version of
the serialization *and* the complexity inherent to
`kotlinx.serialization` with the concept of annotations, surrogate
serializers, modules, encoders and decoders, etc. On top of that, it
turns out json doesn't come for free since the variations in encoding
between json and binary spills over in various parts of the codebase in
the form of `@Contextual` annotations. In other words the tradeoff
doesn't seem to be worth it.

With custom serialization we get full control of the system, but we have
potentially more code. It turns out that it's actually not that much
(especially if we delegate relevant parts to existing bitcoin/lightning
protocol serializers) and, critically, it's systematic code with few
concepts to be aware of. In fact, there is a good chance that we end up
with less code than what we had before for each serialization version.

One drawback of custom serialization is that, since we can't rely on
reflection, and aren't using a compiler plugin like
`kotlinx.serialization`, the handling of polymorphism isn't very nice.
It's trivial to serialize child classes by prefixing with a
discriminator, but deserializing is another matter, as we have no way
to resolve a class constructor corresponding to a discriminator. As a
result, we can't factor the discriminator<->class correspondance which
means we need to be careful to keep serialization and deserialization
in sync.

Regarding json, I believe that we should still be using
`kotlinx-seriaization`, but in a different, non-intrusive way. We could
define a `json` package with serializers generated using the new
`forClass` attribute of `@Serializable`. This would free our regular
classes of all the annotation mess, and we wouldn't need `@Contextual`
anymore due to only using json. There is a catch though, as we still
need to handle backward compatibility for binary codecs relying on those
annotations. I think we can use the same `forClass` trick to duplicate
the necessary serializers in `vX`.

* revert dual funding changes to v3

When adding support for dual funding, we updated v3 serialization. But
it has never been released, and now we have a brand new v4
serialization, so we will never use v3 for dual funding and can revert
those changes.

* make v2/v3 serialization read-only

Older serialization scheme should only be used to read older data, not
to write. We can remove all conversions from _live_ to _mirror_ classes,
and serialization functions.

NB: non-reg tests have been removed and will be added back later. We
didn't check v2 data.

* add json support and non-reg tests

* clean up annotations from the codebase

Now that we have non-reg tests, we can clean up our codebase by removing
all serialization-related annotations from our main classes, and define
external serializers in the `serialization` and `json` packages. There
is some duplication, but it will allow us to easily remove a
serialization version in the future, and keeps our main classes
annotation-free.

The following classes have been left untouched:
- `CltvExpiry`/`CltvExpiryDelta`/`ShortChannelId`: because they have a
  private attribute that prevent external serializer generation. Btw,
  setting `MilliSatoshi.msat` private (as it should be) would break
  `v2`/`v3` serialization for the same reason.
- `Feature`, `TransactionWithInputInfo` and all their subclasses,
  because we would have to define a serializer for every single one of
  them in `v2`, `v3` and `json`, as well as manual `polymorphic`
  declarations in `SerializersModule` of each of those packages. The
  kotlin compiler plugin does a lot of heavy lifting for `sealed class`.
  I did that work for `LightningMessage` because it was worth it to
  clean up those classes.

* introduce a PersistedChannelState state

Not all `ChannelStateWithCommitments` are persisted, for example
`Offline`, `Syncing` are not.

There is a potential backward incompatibility on old serialized data for
`ErrorInformationLeak` (which I'm not tagging as
`PersistedChannelState`), but we shouldn't have any.

Note that in eclair `Closed` isn't peristed either, but I left it here
because it does make sense, and that would certainly cause backward
compat issues anyway.

* remove legacy FundingLocked from wire package

We duplicate the class in `v2`/`v3`. There is no need to do fancy
backward compat with class names, because we never used the class in a
polymorphic way, it was always referenced directly, not by a super
class.

* serialize all ChannelState

So the caller doesn't have to worry about what ChannelState is
serializable. We use a placeholder serializer for remaining channel
states.

Message:
Implement "anchor outputs" commitments (#112)

* Add a new "anchor outputs" type of Commitments format

* Cleanup and move test vectors to their own resource file

* Always use the anchor_outputs commitment format

Legacy format code is removed.

* Make sighash parameter mandatory

* Don't require anchor_outputs support on connnection

We set our feature bit to optional, but still require that channels opened to use are anchor_outputs channels (this
check is done later).
This will allow our peer to open anchor_outputs channels to Phoenix without advertising it in their init message.
